text_or_excerpt: Post: "Do you think West Bengal needs a new political party?" Comment: "No. The people will not change overnight under a new flag." (translated, as published in the paper's Table 1)
reason: Topic is electoral politics; no romantic dyad is present at all, so no RF BehaviorOntology label applies regardless of mapping quality. Included to document that BenSyc is a general Bengali social-discourse corpus, not a relationship-specific one -- only a subset of its content concerns romantic relationships.

text_or_excerpt: Post: "Is BCS actually worth it in Bangladesh?" Comment: "Yes, if your long-term goal is staying here." (translated, as published)
reason: Career-advice topic (BCS = Bangladesh Civil Service exam); no dyad present.

text_or_excerpt: Post: "How do you forget someone you loved?" Comment (translated): "It won't happen... you can't detach in this lifetime."
reason: Bystander commiseration about a breakup: resigned solidarity rather than acknowledgment of a specific stated feeling. Does not clearly clear RF's inclusion bar ('явное признание эмоции или позиции партнёра') because no particular emotion of the poster's is named or paraphrased, and the speaker is not the ex-partner. Illustrates that BenSyc's Support/Validation split (defined by whether the response endorses the poster's interpretation) does not line up cleanly with RF's single Validation construct either way.

text_or_excerpt: Post: "Studying in Bangladesh is a scam." Comment: "All around the world."
reason: This is agreement with a factual/generalized claim about the world, not acknowledgment of an emotion or personal experience. Shows BenSyc's Validation can target propositional agreement -- a case RF's B.VALIDATION (defined strictly around acknowledging the partner's feeling or position as understandable) would not code as validation at all if the same words were said to a partner about a claim rather than a feeling.

text_or_excerpt: Post: "My girlfriend is ghosting me." Comment: "Start posting pictures with other girls."
reason: A third party advises a retaliatory/manipulative tactic against the poster's own partner. RF's BehaviorOntology only codes what one partner observably does to or with the other inside the dyad; it has no construct for an outside advisor coaching retaliation, and B.BLAME_CRITICISM cannot apply because the target of the advice is the partner, not something the speaker says directly to the partner.

text_or_excerpt: "Do you have girlfriends? Set times to hang out with them... It makes you a better, more interesting partner..."
reason: Advice-giving by a bystander responding to a Reddit post; RF has no ADVICE construct at all (see crosswalk row 'Practical Advice').

text_or_excerpt: "...you could say 'I'm really unhappy in this situation where you've made these friends that you can hang out with all day... I don't want to date a guy who can't figure out how to include me in his life and friendships.'" (advisor's suggested script for the poster to say to her boyfriend)
reason: The advisor scripts a hypothetical line for the poster to say TO her boyfriend. If that scripted line were ever actually spoken inside the relationship, it reads as a generalizing character judgment ('a guy who can't figure out how to include me') blended with an implicit change demand -- exactly RF's blame/pressure confusable pair -- but as given it is advice about a possible future utterance, not an observed exchange, so it cannot be coded without the hypothetical actually being said. Flags a possible future use: advisor-suggested scripts could themselves be BehaviorOntology-coded as a quality check on suggested phrasing (a RESPONSE_EVAL use case), independent of whether the dataset is cleared for that use.
One-line dismissive joke from a bystander in response to the poster's sexual-frequency concern; not partner speech.

text_or_excerpt: "Congratulations OP you are a scumbag. But don't worry there are plenty of us out here... Don't stick your dick in taken women. It's easy."
reason: Surface form (blunt, generalizing character attack -- 'you are a scumbag') matches B.BLAME_CRITICISM's marker set closely, but the speaker is an anonymous stranger addressing the poster about the poster's own admitted conduct, not the poster's romantic partner -- RF's directionality field (other_directed = toward one's own partner) does not fit. Useful as a reminder that BLAME_CRITICISM's textual markers are not partner-exclusive; the RF label's dyad-only scope is a project design choice, not a property of the language itself.

text_or_excerpt: "20 and 22 is no problem at all. A typical age range to be in when in a relationship... It's a super common scenario."
reason: Generic reassurance-by-normalization, not tied to acknowledging any specific feeling the poster stated (the poster did not describe distress about the age gap itself). Same Support/Validation looseness identified in the BenSyc entries above: RF's B.VALIDATION requires acknowledging a stated emotion or position, and this comment does neither -- it reassures about a fact pattern instead.

text_or_excerpt: "I swear we're fast getting to the point where we're going to see 'is 3 months too much of an age gap' on here."
reason: Sarcastic dismissal of the legitimacy/seriousness of the poster's concern itself (implies the question is trivial and part of an absurd trend), without any generalizing personal attack on the poster. This is the clearest example found in this research of 'treating a concern as illegitimate' via mockery rather than direct criticism -- the exact phenomenon named in the task's dedicated Invalidation investigation. No current RF label fits: not B.BLAME_CRITICISM (no generalization, and not partner-directed even if it were), and coding it none_observed loses a real, recurring pattern. See the Invalidation section of the main report.

text_or_excerpt: "You need to fall in love with yourself again. Simple. I once went through a heartbreak that hurt me..."
reason: Self-disclosure plus generic encouragement; no acknowledgment of a specific feeling the poster stated. Illustrates that ESConv's 'Self-Disclosure' strategy (see crosswalk) also has no RF analogue -- this is an independent example of the same gap.

Dismissive one-liner mocking the poster's plan before it is even tried -- same illegitimation-via-mockery pattern as example_id-222-comment_2, again with no partner present and no generalizing attack.
